 ::COMMON JUDGMENT::

Petitioners in both the cases have filed these petitions against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 Shilpa.S vs Shilpa.N on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131038697/
2 of M.V.Act for the relief of compensation.

Since, these two cases are arising out of the same incident, hence these cases are clubbed together as per order dated 21.03.2024, accordingly MVC No.3867/2023 is clubbed with original MVC No.3866/2023 and common evidence came to be recorded in the said cases.
Hence, proceeded in these cases to pass the common judgment.

3. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner in both the cases is as under:
 That on 11.05.2023 at about 2.20 p.m. one Ramanjinappa T.A. had been driving autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-40-4207 and petitioner in MVC No.3867/2023 who is none other than wife of Ramanjinappa T.A. was also proceeding in the said autorickshaw near Beechaganahalli Cross, Gudibande Taluk, Chickballapura, at that time, a private car bearing  5 MVC No.3867/2023  C/w. MVC No.3866/2023  SCCH-5 Reg. No.KA-04-ME-5199 driven the said car at high speed in rash and negligent manner from behind and hit the said autorickshaw, due to the tremendous impact the said auto turtles on the road and both Ramanjinappa and petitioner in MVC No.3867/2023 have fell down and Shilpa.S vs Shilpa.N on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131038697/
3 sustained injuries, out of the said accident,
Ramanjinappa died on the spot.
The dead body was shifted to Government Hospital, Bagepalli, wherein death was confirmed and post mortem was done at Taluk Hospital, Gudibande and body was handed over to the family of the deceased.

Further petitioners have spent an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, conveyance,
funeral ceremonies and other charges.

4. Immediately after the accident, petitioner in MVC No.3867/2023 was taken to Bagepalli Government Hospital for first aid, thereafter she was shifted to District  6 MVC No.3867/2023  C/w. MVC No.3866/2023  SCCH-5 Hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein she took treatment as inpatient, for which she has spent an amount of Rs.20,000/- towards treatment, medicines, nourishment and conveyance.
 5. At the time of the accident,
deceased/Ramanjinappa T.A. was aged about 36 years,
working as Security Guard-cum-auto driver, thereby earning Rs.28,000/- p.m. (Rs.18,000/- p.m. from security guard work and Rs.10,000/- from auto driver job).
Due to sudden death of the deceased, petitioners have deprived of the contribution of the deceased.

Further petitioner in MVC No.3867/2023 is housewife,
doing all the routine day-to-day household work.

Due to Shilpa.S vs Shilpa.N on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131038697/
4 the accidental injuries, she is unable to do her work regularly.
C/w. MVC No.3866/2023  SCCH-5  6.

Out of this accident, crime No.58/2023 is registered against the driver of the private car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ME-5199 before the Gudibande Police Station for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.

Respondent No.1 is the owner,
respondent No.2 being the insured and respondent No.3 being the insurer of the said offending car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence,
prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- and Rs.3,00,000/- respectively.

7. On service of notice, respondent No.1 and 2 being owner and insured of the private car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-ME-5199 have appeared through their counsel and filed written statement denying entire averments of the petition.

Further admitted issuance of insurance policy by respondent No.3 in favour of private car bearing  8 MVC No.3867/2023  C/w. MVC No.3866/2023  SCCH-5 Reg. No.KA-04-ME-5199 vide package policy No.820154445 valid from 01.02.2023 to 31.01.2024.
Further submitted that, the driver of the said car had Shilpa.S vs Shilpa.N on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131038697/
5 valid driving licence to drive LMV, MCWG only and said car had valid registration certificate, fitness certificate and permit.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
8. Respondent No.3/insurer of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ME-5199 has appeared before the tribunal and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further denied involvement of the said car in the alleged accident and petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties for the adjudication of the petition and driver of the autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-40-4207 has driven the vehicle without having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Respondent No.3 has admitted  9 MVC No.3867/2023  C/w. MVC No.3866/2023  SCCH-5 issuance of policy of insurance in respect of the said car valid for the period from 01.02.2023 to 31.01.2024,
however the liability to pay the compensation of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further respondent No.3 is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Compensation claimed by the petitioners is on higher side.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition in both the cases.

6 parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
 ::ISSUES IN MVC No.3866/2023::
 1.

Whether Petitioners prove that,
 deceased Ramanjinappa. T.A. died in  the motor vehicle accident that  occurred on 11.05.2023 at about  2.20 p.m. when deceased was driving  10 MVC No.3867/2023  C/w. MVC No.3866/2023  SCCH-5  autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-40-  4207 near Beechaganahalli Cross,
 Gudibande, Chikkaballapura, at that  time, Private Car bearing Reg. No.KA-  04-ME-5199 driven by its driver in a  rash and negligent manner dashed  against the deceased autorickshaw  and caused accident, as mentioned in  claim petition?
 2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for  compensation? If so how much and  from whom?
3. What order or award?

1. Whether Petitioner proves that, she has  sustained grievous injuries in the  motor vehicle accident that occurred  on 11.05.2023 at about 2.20 p.m.
 when petitioner was going in  autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-40-  4207 near Beechaganahalli Cross,
 Chikkaballapura, at that time, one  Private Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ME-  5199 driven by its driver in a rash and  negligent manner dashed against the  petitioner's auto and caused accident,

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about causing death of the accidental injuries to one Ramanjinappa and causing injuries to petitioner in MVC No.3867/2023 out of the accident held on 11.05.2023 at about 2.20 p.m. while they were travelling in autorickshaw bearing Reg. Chikkaballapura.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.
The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the offending car.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners,
this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative in both the cases.

To prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar cards of petitioner No.1 to 4 along with aadhar card of the deceased which are marked as Ex.P.11 it reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Ramanjinappa T.A.,
hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

19. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 4 to 6, then 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/4th of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590  of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s.
 Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear  that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly  income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case  of self employed person or person having fixed salary as  future prospects.

The Petitioners in MVC No.3866/2023 are entitled for compensation of Rs.29,92,160/- (Rupees Twenty Nine Lakhs Ninety Two Thousand One Hundred Sixty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

The Respondent No.3 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order, in both the cases.
The Petitioners in MVC No.3866/2023 are entitled for compensation at the ratio 60:10:10:20 in the award amount.

The Petitioner No.1 and 4 in MVC No.3866/2023 are entitled to get release 60% of their share in award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts by obtaining the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The petitioner in MVC No.3867/2023 is entitled to get release entire award amount through C/w. MVC No.3866/2023 SCCH-5 e-payment directly to her account by obtaining Bank details.
Since Petitioner No.2 and 3 in MVC No.3866/2023 are minors, on deposit of the award amount, their entire share shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank till they attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor Petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor Petitioners.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- in each case.
Keep the original judgment and award in MVC No.3866/2023 and copy of the same in MVC No.3867/2023.
Draw award accordingly.
